rationale: Fresh deployment dominates despite broader stress signals.
Regional and dependency failure should still route to failover.
Capacity exhaustion with healthy dependencies should scale out.
Single-node degradation without regional failure should drain a node.
Write path loss remains the dominant safe response.
Rollback, failover, and readonly all compete; no single audited action covers the incident.
Cross-cutting medium-severity failures do not map cleanly to one audited action.
Mild lag alone is below the audited action boundary.
Regional and service degradation jointly suggest multiple coordinated remediations.
Capacity, write-path, and regional issues create an unsupported mixed failure mode.
A service-local outage with restart headroom should still map to restart_service at the edge of the restart budget.
Demand-driven latency with low capacity headroom should continue to resolve to scale_out.
A write-path outage with sustained lag should still degrade into readonly mode when failover is unavailable.
Missing write-path availability leaves the support boundary undefined and should fail closed.
Out-of-range numeric telemetry should be rejected before the selector extrapolates.
Unexpected extra telemetry should remain outside the audited schema unless the registry is revised.
Mid-band replica skew with service-local degraded behavior should still restart the service rather than drain a node or force readonly mode.
A node-scoped degradation at the replica-skew boundary should still drain the hot node.
Conflicting service scope, write-path loss, and node-like replica skew should remain unsupported rather than forcing a single audited action.
Out-of-range replica skew should fail schema validation before the selector extrapolates.
A region failover remains supported when quorum is degraded but the control plane is still available and no coordinated runbook is required.
High cross-region read staleness with a degraded control plane should still route into readonly mode when coordinated intervention is not required.
Lost quorum and unavailable control plane should force a human page when the operator can still respond inside the mitigation window.
A coordinated regional response still pages a human even when the control plane has not fully disappeared.
Failover-ready regional outages remain unsupported when the control plane is unavailable and human escalation is too slow to be feasible.
Readonly is no longer supported once quorum is lost and coordinated intervention is required, but the regional handoff path is still unavailable on service-scoped incidents.
Missing control-plane availability should fail schema validation before the selector extrapolates into a regional coordination action.
Unexpected quorum-health labels should remain outside the audited schema until the registry is revised.
